title: Have you ever seen a whale?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: time when a situation starts to change, especially in a positive way
skilful at using media outlets, like TV and newspapers, to convey a message to the public

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好，这里是 BBC Learning English 的《6 Minute English》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Phil. And I'm Georgie. Encountering an animal in its natural habitat is a magical experience.
sentences.zh: 我是 Phil。我是 Georgie。在动物的自然栖息地邂逅它们，是一种奇妙的体验。

sentences.en: Have you ever seen an animal in the wild, Georgie?
sentences.zh: Georgie，你在野外见过什么动物吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I have actually. I was on a walk and we saw a baby badger.
sentences.zh: 其实见过。有一次我在散步的时候，我们看到了一只小獾。

sentences.en: It was on its own and it was really cute.
sentences.zh: 它当时是自己一个，特别可爱。

sentences.en: What about you, Phil? Ooh, the most impressive one I've ever seen is actually a whale.
sentences.zh: 你呢，Phil？哦，我见过最令人印象深刻的其实是一头鲸鱼。

sentences.en: I was driving by the coast in Patagonia and you could see them in the sea.
sentences.zh: 当时我开车经过巴塔哥尼亚的海岸，能看到它们在海里。

sentences.en: Well, that sounds amazing. And funny you say that because whale watching has become popular in many coastal parts of the world.
sentences.zh: 听起来真是太棒了。说起来也巧，如今观鲸活动已经在世界上许多沿海地区流行起来。

sentences.en: But watching whales is very different from what humans used to do to: hunt and kill them for their oil and meat – an activity known as whaling.
sentences.zh: 但观鲸和人类过去对鲸鱼的所作所为截然不同：人类曾经为了鲸油和鲸肉去捕杀它们，这项活动被称为捕鲸(whaling)。

sentences.en: Last year marked the 40th anniversary of the International Whaling Commission's global moratorium – that's a temporary ban on the commercial killing of whales.
sentences.zh: 去年是国际捕鲸委员会全球暂禁令(moratorium)实施 40 周年——这是一项对商业捕鲸的临时禁令。

sentences.en: Although Japan, Iceland and Norway continue to hunt whales, there's no doubt the ban has saved many whales species from extinction.
sentences.zh: 尽管日本、冰岛和挪威仍在继续捕鲸，但毫无疑问，这项禁令已经让许多鲸鱼物种免于灭绝。

sentences.en: In this programme, we'll discuss our past and present relationship with these giants of the ocean.
sentences.zh: 在这期节目中，我们要聊聊人类与这些海洋巨兽之间过去和现在的关系。

sentences.en: And, as usual, we'll learn some useful new words and phrases too.
sentences.zh: 像往常一样，我们也会学习一些实用的新单词和短语。

sentences.en: Plus, you'll find all the vocabulary for this episode, along with a quiz and worksheet, on our website: bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 此外，本期节目的所有词汇，以及配套的小测验和练习题，都可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到。

sentences.en: But first, I have a question for you, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 不过首先，Georgie，我有个问题要考考你。

sentences.en: You probably know that the world's largest whale is the blue whale, growing up to 30m long, but which whale species is the smallest?
sentences.zh: 你可能知道，世界上最大的鲸鱼是蓝鲸，体长可达 30 米，但最小的鲸鱼物种是什么呢？

sentences.en: Is it: a) the beluga whale, b) the vaquita whale, or c) the pygmy right whale?
sentences.zh: 是 a) 白鲸？b) 小头鼠海豚？还是 c) 小露脊鲸？

sentences.en: Hmm. Well, 'pygmy' makes me think small so I'm going to go with c) the pygmy right whale.
sentences.zh: 嗯，'pygmy'这个词让我想到'小'，所以我选 c) 小露脊鲸。

sentences.en: OK. We'll find out later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好，答案我们会在节目后面揭晓。

sentences.en: Humans have hunted whales for at least a thousand years, starting with small groups of hunters in slow-moving wooden boats.
sentences.zh: 人类捕鲸的历史至少有一千年，最初是小群猎人乘坐行驶缓慢的木船进行捕猎。

sentences.en: Catching whales like this was often unsuccessful, especially big whales like blue and humpback whales, which can swim up to 30km/hr.
sentences.zh: 这样的捕鲸方式往往难以成功，尤其是对蓝鲸、座头鲸这类大型鲸鱼来说，它们的游速最快可达每小时 30 公里。

sentences.en: But all that changed in the late 1800s, as Jayne Pierce of the South Georgia Heritage Trust explained to BBC Radio 4 programme Rare Earth:
sentences.zh: 但到了 19 世纪末，这一切都改变了，南乔治亚遗产信托基金的 Jayne Pierce 向 BBC 广播四台节目《Rare Earth》做了如下解释：

sentences.en: And that was a turning point for the whale.
sentences.zh: 这对鲸鱼来说是一个转折点(turning point)。

sentences.en: The whale couldn't stand a chance. In 1870, a chap – that's an informal word for a man – called Svend Foyn invented the exploding harpoon, a weapon for killing whales.
sentences.zh: 鲸鱼从此毫无胜算(couldn't stand a chance)。1870 年，一个叫 Svend Foyn 的家伙(chap，这是对'男人'的非正式说法)发明了爆炸鱼叉——一种用来捕杀鲸鱼的武器。

sentences.en: This was a turning point. The phrase turning point means a time when a situation starts to change, especially in a positive way, although sadly not in this case.
sentences.zh: 这就是一个转折点。turning point 这个短语指的是某种情况开始发生变化的时刻，通常是朝着积极的方向，不过很遗憾，在这里并非如此。

sentences.en: After this, the whales didn't stand a chance, meaning they had no chance of successfully avoiding the hunters.
sentences.zh: 自此之后，鲸鱼便毫无胜算(didn't stand a chance)，也就是说，它们再也没有机会成功躲避猎人的追捕。

sentences.en: Foyn's exploding harpoon, added to the invention of faster steam-powered boats, increased whaling massively throughout the 20th century, to the point where over three million whales had been killed and many species faced extinction.
sentences.zh: Foyn 发明的爆炸鱼叉，再加上速度更快的蒸汽动力船只的问世，使得整个 20 世纪的捕鲸活动大幅增加，以至于超过 300 万头鲸鱼惨遭捕杀，许多物种也因此濒临灭绝。

sentences.en: By the 1970s, there were only a few great whales left and environmental groups like Greenpeace started the Save the Whales campaign to make people aware of devastation in whale populations and the cruelty of whaling.
sentences.zh: 到了 20 世纪 70 年代，大型鲸鱼所剩无几，绿色和平组织(Greenpeace)等环保团体发起了'拯救鲸鱼'(Save the Whales)运动，以唤起人们对鲸鱼种群遭受重创以及捕鲸行为残忍性的关注。

sentences.en: It became popular to listen to the Song of the Whale, recordings of whales communicating at sea, which sound something like this:
sentences.zh: 聆听'鲸之歌'(Song of the Whale)一度成为风尚——那是鲸鱼在海中交流的录音，听起来大概是这样的：

sentences.en: Here's marine biologist Joe Roman, discussing the Save the Whales campaign with BBC Radio 4's Rare Earth: People started thinking about whales in different ways.
sentences.zh: 下面是海洋生物学家 Joe Roman 在 BBC 广播四台《Rare Earth》节目中谈到'拯救鲸鱼'运动：人们开始以不同的方式看待鲸鱼。

sentences.en: And then we have to give a shout-out to activist groups like Greenpeace, who put their RIB boats – they put their Zodiacs in between Soviet hunting vessels and sperm whales.
sentences.zh: 在这里我们也不得不为绿色和平这样的行动团体点个赞(shout-out)，他们把自己的充气艇——他们的 Zodiac 快艇——直接开到苏联捕鲸船和抹香鲸之间。

sentences.en: And they were very good at media. Joe gives a shout-out to Greenpeace activists for protecting whales.
sentences.zh: 而且他们非常擅长运用媒体。Joe 为保护鲸鱼的绿色和平行动者们点赞(shout-out)。

sentences.en: To give a shout-out to someone means to praise them in public.
sentences.zh: give a shout-out to someone 意思是公开赞扬某人。

sentences.en: Videos and photos taken by Greenpeace changed public opinion about whaling.
sentences.zh: 绿色和平拍摄的视频和照片改变了公众对捕鲸的看法。

sentences.en: Joe says Greenpeace were good at media, meaning they skilfully used media outlets like TV and newspapers to convey their message to the public.
sentences.zh: Joe 说绿色和平很擅长运用媒体(good at media)，意思是他们巧妙地利用电视、报纸等媒体渠道，向公众传达自己的信息。

sentences.en: Many whale species are still endangered and all whales still face danger from ocean acidification and plastic pollution.
sentences.zh: 如今仍有许多鲸鱼物种处于濒危状态，而且所有鲸鱼仍然面临着海洋酸化和塑料污染的威胁。

sentences.en: But the moratorium – that means the temporary suspension – on hunting them has lasted 40 years and hopefully will help protect whales for decades more.
sentences.zh: 但针对捕鲸的暂禁令(moratorium，即临时中止)已经持续了 40 年，希望它还能在未来几十年里继续为保护鲸鱼发挥作用。

sentences.en: OK. Phil, isn't it time you revealed the answer to your question?
sentences.zh: 好了，Phil，是不是该公布你那个问题的答案了？

sentences.en: OK. I asked you which was the smallest species of whale.
sentences.zh: 好，我问你最小的鲸鱼物种是什么。

sentences.en: And I said the pygmy right whale, didn't I?
sentences.zh: 我说的是小露脊鲸，对吧？

sentences.en: You did. Unfortunately, the answer is actually the vaquita whale, which is about 1.5m long.
sentences.zh: 没错。不过很遗憾，正确答案其实是小头鼠海豚，体长约 1.5 米。

sentences.en: Oh, so cute! OK. Let's recap the rest of the vocabulary we've learned.
sentences.zh: 哦，真可爱！好，我们来回顾一下剩下的词汇。

sentences.en: A chap is an informal word for a man. A turning point is when a situation starts to change, especially for the better.
sentences.zh: chap 是对'男人'的非正式说法。turning point(转折点)指的是某种情况开始发生变化的时刻，通常是朝着好的方向。

sentences.en: If someone doesn't stand a chance, they have no chance of success.
sentences.zh: 如果某人 doesn't stand a chance，意思就是他毫无成功的可能。

sentences.en: To give a shout-out to someone means topublicly praise them.
sentences.zh: give a shout-out to someone 意思是公开赞扬某人。

sentences.en: And finally,if you're good at media, you are skilful at using media outlets to convey a message to the public.
sentences.zh: 最后，如果你 good at media(擅长运用媒体)，意思是你很擅长利用媒体渠道向公众传达信息。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up but remember you can find worksheets, quizzes and loads more resources to improve your English on our website: bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 六分钟又到了，别忘了，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到练习题、小测验，以及更多帮助你提升英语水平的资源。

sentences.en: See you there soon but for now, it's goodbye!
sentences.zh: 我们网站上见，不过现在，先说再见啦！

sentences.en: Bye!
sentences.zh: 拜拜！
